title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 4: mark of vessels, not cause — seal of adoption / flight from iniquity
pass_a_gloss: For he, in the aforesaid place, does not teach from what cause vessels are elected unto glory, but by what mark they are discerned. And he says a twofold mark is impressed on them: One, which is perceptible to God alone, namely the seal of eternal adoption, The Lord knoweth them that are his. The other, which is open to men, namely flight from impiety, and the practice of sanctity and justice; Let him depart from iniquity: If he shall have cleansed himself, he shall be a vessel unto honour.
pass_b_english: In that place Paul does not teach why vessels are elect to glory, but by what mark they are known. He stamps a double mark on them: one God alone can read — the seal of eternal adoption ("The Lord knows who are his"); the other men can see — flight from impiety and the practice of holiness and justice ("Let him depart from iniquity"; "If he cleanses himself, he will be a vessel unto honour").
source_text: Nam ille, in loco praedicto, non docet ex qua causa eligantur vasa ad gloriam, sed qua nota discernantur. Duplicem autem notam illis impressam dicit: Unam, quae Deo soli perceptibilis est, nempe signaculum aeternae adoptionis, Novit Deus qui sunt sui. Alteram, quae hominibus patet, fugam scilicet impietatis, & praxim sanctitatis & justitiae; Recedat ab iniquitate: Si se emundaverit, erit vas in honorem.
